purpose: Catch recommendation failures where a plausible taste hypothesis is not carried into real product candidates, page-level teaser prices are mistaken for the selected option price, or later user corrections fail to update ranking. Also catch fresh-produce recommendation failures where one preference axis is treated as sufficient, the user's own desired candidates are implicitly excluded, search stays inside a narrow marketplace surface, or products with little direct evidence are promoted as top taste picks.

scenario.initial_request: 온라인에서 살 수 있는 삼겹살이나 오겹살을 추천해 줘. 지방의 고소함이 중심이고 육향은 약간 있으면 좋다.

objective_slots: very cheap but not notably bad

scenario.assistant_hypothesis_example: A Berkshire-type pork product may fit the stated taste preference.
scenario.later_user_correction: 2500원대도 쓸데없이 비싸다고 생각해서 보통 2000원대 또는 그 이하를 먹는다.

normalized_constraint_after_correction.over_cap_policy: Only keep above-cap candidates as explicit exceptions with strong evidence and user-visible justification.

fixed_product_fixtures.page_title: 삼겹살 / 오겹살 / 듀록 삼겹살 / 듀록 오겹살 2kg
fixed_product_fixtures.regression_trap: Do not report 1345 KRW/100g for the selected Duroc option.
Do not omit ordinary low-price candidates merely because a breed hypothesis sounds more premium.

assistant_failure_pattern: Treats 물복 as if it fully determines sweetness, acidity, aroma, variety preference, and desired product.
Moves directly to purchasable products without checking whether another taste axis could materially change the winner.
Never leaves room for a specific variety, farm, region, or product the user already wants to try.
Searches only easy-to-find large-marketplace listings and misses materially different specialist or producer-direct channels.
Ranks a zero-review or otherwise weak-direct-evidence listing as the best-tasting or personal top pick while stronger-evidence alternatives exist.
expected_behavior: Do not infer unrelated taste preferences from texture preference alone.
If another unanswered preference axis could materially flip the recommendation, ask only the highest-value 1-2 follow-up questions rather than stopping after texture.

Before closing the candidate pool, leave room for a concrete variety, farm, region, seller, or product the user may already want to try; proceed with a stated default if the user asks not to be questioned.

For fresh produce where seller, lot, harvest timing, selection, and shipping can materially affect quality, inspect more than one seller/channel type when feasible, including specialist or producer-direct sources rather than only large marketplaces.
Do not use review count as a quality score, but do not promote a product with almost no direct product-level evidence to a strong top-taste recommendation over better-supported alternatives.
If all surviving products have weak direct evidence, lower confidence or say evidence is insufficient instead of fabricating a precise taste ranking.

required_behavior: If a breed, brand, product class, or method is presented as a taste-fit hypothesis, inspect at least one concrete candidate from that hypothesis or explicitly state that no candidate survived the constraints.
Collect a reasonably broad candidate pool before narrowing on the taste hypothesis.
For each recommended purchasable product, bind price claims to the exact selected option or SKU rather than the page-level base price.
Include option surcharge, selected weight or quantity, and current availability in the verification chain before presenting normalized unit price as verified.
Preserve the two objective slots instead of collapsing cheap-value and taste-value into one score.
After the user lowers the practical price ceiling, rerank or remove earlier candidates that conflict with the new ceiling.
Use a direct product detail page when a link is presented as the purchase link.
In subjective recommendations, do not treat one answered preference axis as sufficient when another still-unknown axis could materially flip the top candidates.
Do not silently translate a texture preference such as soft peach into sweetness, acidity, aroma, variety, farm, or brand preference.

Before closing a subjective shopping candidate pool, preserve the possibility that the user already has a concrete variety, seller, region, brand, or product they want considered; if the user requests no questions, proceed with explicit reasonable defaults.

When seller or distribution channel can materially affect quality, broad search means inspecting materially different seller/channel types when feasible, not merely collecting several listings from one marketplace surface.

For sensory quality claims that specifications cannot establish, seek direct product-level evidence close to the current product or selling lot. Review count alone is not quality, but a candidate with almost no direct evidence should not receive a strong top-taste ranking over better-supported alternatives without another strong direct basis.
fail_conditions: States that Berkshire is the best taste fit but never inspects a Berkshire candidate and never explains why it was excluded.
Uses the page base price for a selected option with a surcharge.
Recommends before exact option price or availability is verified.
Keeps 2400-2500 KRW/100g products as ordinary top picks after the user makes 2000 KRW/100g the practical ceiling.
Searches only the inferred premium breed or brand class and misses materially cheaper ordinary candidates.
Provides only a search-results or category link while presenting it as the exact product link.
After learning only that the user likes soft peaches, assumes strong sweetness, low acidity, or a particular variety without asking or marking the assumption.
Closes the recommendation pool without leaving room for a specific variety, farm, region, seller, or product the user may already want considered.
For fresh produce, searches only one easy large-marketplace surface despite materially relevant specialist or producer-direct channels being feasible to inspect.

Ranks a zero-review or otherwise direct-evidence-poor product as the strongest taste recommendation while better-supported alternatives exist, solely because the listing title matches the inferred preference.
